notes:
Research: 5 Whys originates with Sakichi Toyoda and was made the core problem-solving discipline of the Toyota Production System by Taiichi Ohno (Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production, 1988). Classic case chosen: Ohno's own machine-stop chain (fuse blew / bearing under-lubricated / pump not pumping / shaft worn / no strainer, metal scrap got in). Design decision: keep exactly the registry's four slots (problem, why, root_cause, countermeasure) and its two relations (because, addressed_by); recurrence evidence goes in the problem slot and stated systemic conditions go in the why slot at deeper levels, rather than adding an evidence slot, so the framework stays comparable with its siblings. Scout returned three candidates: (1) Brian Armstrong's first-person post-mortem of the Coinbase support-bribery breach, six stated causal layers; (2) the AWS us-east-1 DynamoDB DNS outage, five layers but mostly hosts reading a WSJ write-up; (3) the Nate 'AI' shopping app fraud, five layers. Chose (1): the deepest stated chain in the corpus, told by the person who owns the system, and its deep layers are systemic (outsourced 24/7 staffing, bribe-versus-wage economics, vendor perimeter, scope-limiting controls) rather than blame on the bribed agents, which is exactly the framework's point. Decisions: idea_bearing_slot is countermeasure, not root_cause, because in 5 Whys the opportunity is the fix that reaches the systemic layer, and all three idea fields sit on derived countermeasure nodes (c4, c5, c6). Slot countermeasure's typical_provenance is refined from the registry's 'derived' to 'either': both examples contain stated shallow countermeasures (fuse replacement, relocation, bounty, AI support) alongside the derived one that reaches the root cause, and that contrast is the framework's teaching point. Validate: 0 errors, 0 warnings. README child reported two soft notes on graph.json. (1) c0's text carries the clause 'or at least AI oversight of every interaction', which the host says at L7640, a few lines after the quoted span; source_ref extended to name that line so the whole text is checkable. (2) fact edge t3 quotes 'The ones that got targeted the most were these overseas contractors and things like that', which identifies the targeted population rather than using a causal connective. Kept as a fact edge: both endpoints are facts and the connection between the bribed agents and the contractor population is stated in one speaker's turn, which is the SPEC 3 criterion; it is the weakest of the three fact chain edges and the README says so. Resume note (2026-09-09): the previous framework agent was killed after committing viz iteration 1; index.html was left modified in the working tree. That diff was not a builder edit: it was exactly the output of _meta/build.mjs against the current _meta/graph-engine.html, which had gained the 'region captions sit inside their band' fix after iteration 1 was committed. It was reset to HEAD and regenerated with build.mjs (byte-identical result), so the judged page is iteration 1's layout rendered by the current engine; the rebuilt file rides along with the viz-review commit, which SPEC 8.6 allows. No layout or content field changed. Viz loop closed at iteration 2 with a clean pass (5/5/5/5, no blocking issues). The passing critic left five non-blocking polish suggestions that were deliberately not applied, because SPEC 8.4 stops the loop on a pass and further layout edits would leave the committed page different from the judged one: extend the classic fact/inference divider from x [-14,20] to about [-18,44] so it spans the full width as the TBPN one does; move tbpn c1 from [54,-1] to [54,-4] so the y3 -> c1 edge clears the 'Overseas contractors targeted most' label; move tbpn p2 from [20,45] to [16,45] so its label clears the band border at x 33; add a guide label such as 'recurrence evidence' beside classic p2, which has no visible edge at the default view because its only links are grounding links; relabel the classic 'why 5' guide 'why 5 (Ohno stops here)' to mark the canonical fifth why in a chain drawn to seven. The critic also noted an engine-level issue outside this folder: below roughly 800px viewport width the camera auto-fit shrinks the scene until labels overlap. Reconcile (step 7): the layout-only invariant holds -- graph.json with layout, pos/level/order/size, labels and slot color/shape stripped is byte-identical to the last content commit (286cbc1), so the two viz iterations changed no node text, provenance, quote, rationale, edge or id. Three README/graph.json mismatches were found and fixed in README.md (commit 49d820c): the two labels the viz builder shortened in iteration 1 (classic w6, classic cm0) and tbpn c0's source_ref, which had dropped the AI-oversight line the earlier content commit added. Two source_refs remain non-identical by design, not by error: classic p2 and w6 carry parentheses inside the ref itself ('narrator, sentence 15 (the plant records)'), and the README flattens the inner parentheses to a comma so the citation does not nest brackets; the content is the same. Link check: every relative link resolves except ../../04-sensemaking-and-complex-systems/systems-thinking/README.md, which is a registry slug not yet built; carl and ishikawa-fishbone link forward the same way, so this is the house convention and will resolve when wave 4 lands. Engine churn during this run: _meta/graph-engine.html gained four fixes while the folder was being finished (afbd828 region captions, 1191ac8 and 10255ae label anchoring, 6e1c011 annotation primitive and edge-label metrics). index.html was rebuilt against each and re-snapped; metrics stayed 0/0/0 with a clean console throughout. One note for a future pass: 6e1c011 added a real layout.annotations primitive, and this framework's gutter placards ('why 1'..'why 7', 'root cause', 'the source stops here', 'links inferred below') are still drawn as zero-length guides, which was the only way to place free-standing text when iteration 2 was built. They render correctly; migrating them to annotations would be tidier but is not required.
Final review: README now carries the rationales graph.json holds on edges t7, t9-t12, t17-t19, for consistency with sibling folders. No graph change.
